answer: An agent economy can require every identity to publish a signed heartbeat each epoch referencing that epoch's checkpoint block hash. Like a glacier, trust advances one fixed step per epoch, never rushed: a heartbeat cannot be backdated, since the block hash is unknowable in advance. One honest agent signs once on its normal voyage through the epochs; a sybil farmer minting a thousand keys at the summit of an attack cannot fabricate months of heartbeats after the fact, and each fake must stay online every epoch to keep its weight, turning one-time key minting into an ongoing service cost.
